questions.stem: Sara, 32, is in your GP clinic. Before her headache she had zigzag lights and then numbness in her right hand and face. She takes the combined pill and smokes. You want to tell a migraine aura apart from a TIA. Which question helps most?
options: "Did your eye water or your nose run on that same side during the worst of the pain?"
"Is the headache worse when you cough, strain or bend over?"
"Did the lights and numbness spread gradually over minutes, or start all at once?"
"Have you had any pain in your jaw when you chew?"
questions.why: Tempo and quality separate the two. A migraine aura is positive (lights, tingling) and spreads gradually over 5 minutes or more. A TIA is sudden, negative (numbness, visual loss) and at its worst from the start.
notes: Tearing and rhinorrhoea point to cluster headache. They do not help separate an aura from a TIA.
Pain worse with coughing or straining is a red flag for raised intracranial pressure, not a way to tell aura from TIA.
Jaw claudication screens for temporal arteritis, which almost never occurs under 50. It does not help separate aura from TIA.

questions.stem: Sara, 32, has migraine with aura, a normal neurological examination and a negative urine pregnancy test. She takes a combined oral contraceptive pill, smokes up to 5 cigarettes a day and wants reliable contraception. What is the most appropriate advice about her contraception?
options: Stop the combined pill and switch to an implant, IUD or progestogen-only pill
Keep taking the combined pill continuously to avoid the oestrogen-withdrawal week
Change to the combined vaginal ring to give steadier oestrogen levels
Change to a combined pill with 20 microgram ethinylestradiol
questions.why: Migraine with aura makes any oestrogen-containing contraceptive category 4 (contraindicated) because it raises the risk of ischaemic stroke, and smoking adds to that risk. Progestogen-only and copper methods are safe. She should use condoms until the new method is working.
notes: Continuous use can help menstrual migraine without aura, but it is still oestrogen. It stays contraindicated with aura.
The ring contains ethinylestradiol, so it carries the same stroke risk and the same contraindication as the combined pill.
Lowering the dose does not remove the contraindication. Any combined hormonal method is category 4 in migraine with aura.

questions.stem: Sara, 32, says her zigzag lights started near the centre of her vision and spread outwards over 20 minutes. Next, tingling spread from her right hand to her face over 10 to 15 minutes, and everything resolved before the headache. What best explains this slow spread of aura symptoms?
options: Embolic occlusion moving distally along a branch of the left posterior cerebral artery
Focal epileptiform discharge spreading through the occipital and parietal cortex
Vasospasm of cerebral arteries cutting perfusion below the ischaemic threshold
A wave of neuronal and glial depolarisation spreading across cortex at about 3 mm/min
questions.why: Cortical spreading depolarisation is a slow wave of depolarisation followed by suppression. It travels at 2 to 5 mm/min, so symptoms move across the visual and sensory maps over minutes. Positive features at the leading edge are followed by negative ones, and the wave can activate the trigeminovascular system.
notes: An embolus causes a sudden negative deficit that is worst at onset. It does not cause shimmering lights that move over 20 minutes.
Seizure activity spreads within seconds and gives brief stereotyped symptoms, not a march over 20 minutes followed by a migraine headache.
The old vascular theory has been replaced. Blood flow falls modestly after the depolarisation wave, and it does not reach ischaemic levels during a typical aura.

questions.stem: During today's aura, Sara, 32, had tingling and then numbness that started in her right hand and crept into the right side of her face and lips over 10 to 15 minutes, with no weakness. Where in the brain did this sensory aura most likely arise?
options: Left precentral gyrus, spreading from the hand area towards the face area
Left postcentral gyrus, spreading from the hand area laterally to the face area
Right postcentral gyrus, spreading from the hand area laterally to the face area
Left ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus
questions.why: Right-sided sensory symptoms come from the left primary somatosensory cortex (postcentral gyrus). On the sensory homunculus the face lies lateral and inferior to the hand, so a wave spreading laterally moves the symptoms from the hand to the face.
notes: The precentral gyrus is the primary motor cortex. Aura arising there would cause weakness or jerking, which she did not have.
The somatosensory pathways cross, so the right postcentral gyrus would cause symptoms on the left side, as in her one right-sided attack.
The VPL nucleus relays body sensation only. The face relays through VPM, and a thalamic lesion would not spread across the cortical map over minutes.
